title: Abbott puts the brakes on data center permits
key_facts: Gov. Greg Abbott ordered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to stop issuing data center permits until state officials have fuller answers on grid and water demand (directive of 21 Sep 2026).
TCEQ must align permitting with a review by the Public Utility Commission, ERCOT and the Texas Water Development Board, and report back by 19 Oct.
ERCOT said in August it was considering more than 474 gigawatts of connection requests, more than five times the grid's record peak demand.
In September ERCOT began formal information requests to large-load developers, covering ownership, incentives, onsite generation and community impacts.
A week earlier Abbott told the water board to enforce existing water-use reporting rules on major users including data centers.
The order does not automatically cancel projects; effect depends on which approvals each already has.
Caldwell County projects named: Tract's 3,000-acre Caldwell Valley Technology Park (over 4 GW planned), Prime Data Centers, Edged Energy.
quote_evidence: “Simply put, Texans must come first,” Abbott said in announcing the Sept. 21 directive.
TCEQ has been ordered to report back to Abbott by Oct. 19 on its compliance with the directive.
What Abbott’s directive does not do is automatically cancel those projects
why_it_matters_hint: Texas, the largest state data center market, is tying environmental permits to grid and water audits.
notes: Older news: directive 21 Sep 2026; article published 8 Oct 2026 as a local explainer. Single local outlet.
